# Results — Study 226 (Crude-Seasonality): does crude oil rally every spring? 2000–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly returns of **WTI crude (CL=F)**
and **energy equities (XLE)** plus the **13-week T-bill** (^IRX, the cash leg), built from daily
closes resampled to month-end on a verified hole-free grid: 2000-09 → 2026-05, **309 months**.
As-of 2026-06-01; inputs fingerprint `04d20473b062`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `WEAK` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Every year"? `BUSTED`

The spring-versus-autumn spread in crude is real enough to clear the |t| ≥ 2 bar (t = 2.47 on the
paired spread), so there is something here — but it is far too fragile to trade. No individual month
clears that bar after Bonferroni correction for 12 tests. The spread is insignificant in the
2000–2012 sub-period (t = 1.42) and only marginally significant 2013-on (t = 2.02 in the stronger
half of the data). And the calendar timer built on it is a mirage for energy equities: the XLE timer
earns **+0.7% CAGR / Sharpe 0.04** against buy-and-hold XLE's **+7.8% / Sharpe 0.35**. The crude
timer beats buy-and-hold CL=F (CAGR 12.3% vs 3.8%) but crude is itself a volatile, negative-CAGR
asset in real total-return terms; the timer simply avoids the deepest drawdown months rather than
delivering a robust seasonal edge. `WEAK`, `MIRAGE`.

## Data stamp

- **Pair**: WTI crude (CL=F) + energy equities (XLE) + T-bill (^IRX) monthly, 2000-09 → 2026-05,
  **309 months**, as-of 2026-06-01, fingerprint `04d20473b062`
- **Construction**: daily closes resampled to month-end (last close of each calendar month).
  Grid asserted hole-free on every read by `fetch_data`.

## Per-month CL=F statistics (one-sample t vs 0, n ≈ 26 each)

| Month | Mean | t-stat | n | Signal? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | +2.0% | +1.18 | 26 | No |
| **Feb** | **+3.5%** | **+2.50** | 26 | Nominally — fails Bonferroni |
| Mar | +2.6% | +0.79 | 26 | No |
| Apr | +2.3% | +1.25 | 26 | No |
| May | +3.0% | +0.74 | 26 | No |
| **Jun** | **+3.0%** | **+2.39** | 25 | Nominally — fails Bonferroni |
| Jul | +0.7% | +0.41 | 25 | No |
| Aug | −0.8% | −0.60 | 25 | No |
| Sep | −1.2% | −0.71 | 26 | No |
| Oct | −1.8% | −0.85 | 26 | No |
| Nov | −2.7% | −1.29 | 26 | No |
| Dec | +0.3% | +0.13 | 26 | No |

Two months (Feb, Jun) nominally pass |t| ≥ 2, but Bonferroni correction for 12 simultaneous tests
raises the threshold to |t| ≈ 3 (α = 0.05/12 ≈ 0.004). Neither clears that bar. The spring
narrative is a pattern, not a sharp month-by-month signal.

## Spring vs Autumn spread

| | Mean monthly return | n |
|---|---|---|
| Spring (Apr–Jun) | +2.76% | 77 |
| Autumn (Aug–Nov) | −1.62% | 103 |
| **Spread** | **+4.38%** | — |
| **t-stat** | **2.47** | — |

The direction is as expected (spring positive, autumn negative) and the spread clears |t| ≥ 2 on
the full sample. But it fails both Bonferroni and sub-period robustness.

## Sub-period decay

| Period | Spring mean | Autumn mean | t-stat | n_spring | n_autumn |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2000–2012 | +1.76% | −1.20% | 1.42 | 36 | 51 |
| 2013–on | +3.64% | −2.03% | 2.02 | 41 | 52 |

The signal is confined to the post-shale era (2013-on) — the period dominated by US shale supply
swings that created new seasonal patterns in storage and refinery runs. In the pre-shale decade
(2000–2012) the effect is insignificant (t = 1.42). This is a regime-specific pattern, not an
unconditional seasonal law.

## Calendar timer vs buy-and-hold

Long crude/energy in Apr–Jun, short in Aug–Nov, T-bill otherwise. Sharpe = excess of T-bill, both legs.

| | CAGR | Sharpe (excess) | max-DD |
|---|---|---|---|
| crude timer (CL=F) | +12.3% | 0.46 | −55% |
| buy & hold CL=F | +3.8% | 0.24 | −87% |
| energy timer (XLE) | +0.7% | **0.04** | −57% |
| buy & hold XLE | +7.8% | **0.35** | −64% |

The crude timer outperforms buy-and-hold CL=F, but that comparison is misleading: crude futures
have essentially zero real long-run return (CL=F +3.8% CAGR over 2000–2026), and the timer
mainly avoids the worst drawdown months rather than harvesting a genuine premium. Against energy
equities — the investable asset — the timer is badly dominated: Sharpe 0.04 vs 0.35 for buy-and-hold.

## The honest takeaway

The spring-versus-autumn spread in crude passes the |t| ≥ 2 bar on the full sample (t = 2.47),
earning a `WEAK` signal stamp — but only barely, only after choosing the favourable window, and
with clear regime dependence (insignificant 2000–2012). No individual month clears the
Bonferroni-corrected bar. The calendar timer fails completely on the investable energy-equity
proxy (XLE Sharpe 0.04 vs 0.35 buy-and-hold). `WEAK`, `MIRAGE`.
